name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Thursday 29 June 1972

clue.text: Snipe's Testament or Friar's Lantern?

blocks.note: a will is a last testament
a wisp is the collective noun for a flock of snipe, and the possessive reads as 'of the', shortened to o'

explanation.surface: Two curious old relics, a snipe's will and a friar's lamp, offered as alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'the snipe's testament' as 'the will of the wisp', giving WILL-O'-THE-WISP.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar's lantern is an old country name for the ghostly marsh light also called ignis fatuus.

clue.text: Marriage being its key ceremony

blocks.note: to wed is to go through the marriage ceremony
a key's partner is a lock

explanation.surface: A wedding is presented as the key that unlocks a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the state of being married, a formal synonym for matrimony.

clue.text: Silly fellow, look out! It will catch you

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the word for look sits around the other piece

blocks.note: lo! is an old cry meaning look
an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A warning shouted at a fool who is about to be caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope is thrown to snare a running animal, so it is the thing that catches.

clue.text: Like Endymion, heed no alarm?

blocks.note: surface reading: ignoring a warning, as some classical hero might
setter's reading: Endymion was put into eternal sleep, and the alarm is an alarm clock you fail to wake for

explanation.walkthrough: Endymion is the shepherd of Greek myth granted everlasting sleep; the alarm is the bedside clock, not a danger signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep past the time you meant to wake up is to fail to respond to the morning clock.

clue.text: Evelyn boxed with Pandora

blocks.note: first meaning: Evelyn ... is the dead girl of Robert Browning's poem of that name
second meaning: when Pandora opened her box, the one thing left inside was this

explanation.surface: Someone called Evelyn sparring in the ring alongside Pandora.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxed suggests fighting, but it means shut in a box: Pandora's box.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Browning's Evelyn, and the single blessing remaining in Pandora's jar once the evils escaped.

clue.text: We raise a flower to discover a beastly transformation

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardeners growing a flower and getting a monstrous surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who turns into a wolf undergoes a change into an animal, a monstrous shape-shift.

clue.text: React to a pistol shot on or off track

definitions.text: React to a pistol shot on or off track

blocks.clueFragment: React to a pistol shot on or off track
blocks.note: surface reading: a runner setting off when the gun fires

blocks.clueFragment: React to a pistol shot on or off track
blocks.note: setter's reading: off the track, anyone hearing a gunshot jumps in surprise

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both beginning a race at the gun and jumping with sudden fright.

clue.text: Thrashed as the young shaver should be

definitions.text: as the young shaver should be

blocks.note: first meaning: beaten, given a good hiding

blocks.clueFragment: as the young shaver should be
blocks.note: second meaning: soaped up before a shave, as a young man shaving should be

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned view that a cheeky boy deserves a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: A young shaver is slang for a lad; read literally it is someone shaving, who needs a foam of soap first.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally to give someone a beating, and literally to be covered in shaving foam.

clue.text: Darcy and Joan might qualify for Essex side

blocks.clueFragment: Darcy and Joan might qualify for Essex side
blocks.note: surface reading: two people good enough to be picked for an Essex sports team

blocks.clueFragment: Darcy and Joan might qualify for Essex side
blocks.note: setter's reading: a devoted old couple could win the side of bacon awarded at Dunmow in Essex

explanation.walkthrough: Darcy is presumably a misprint for Darby: Darby and Joan are the proverbial contented old married pair. The Dunmow custom awards a side of bacon to couples who have not quarrelled for a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole side of salted bacon is the prize at the Dunmow trial, held in the county of Essex.

clue.text: But Fido's off-colour with it

blocks.note: surface reading: the dog is unwell because of some illness
setter's reading: the word also names a kind of paint, the very thing that gives a wall colour, so the 'but' makes the contrast

explanation.walkthrough: Fido is the stock name for a dog. The opening 'But' only makes sense once you know the answer is also a paint.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a viral illness of dogs, and also a water-based paint used on walls.

clue.text: Profit from an old tip

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a vail is an archaic word for a gratuity given to a servant

explanation.surface: Making money from an outdated piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip suggests a hint, but it is a gratuity, and 'old' flags an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of benefit or use; as a noun it means advantage, as in 'to no purpose'.

clue.text: Player is carried in the boot perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word is only one possible spelling, so its letters may be rearranged
something carried in a bag sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument travels stowed in the car boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the double-reed woodwind instrument is a musician, a player.

clue.text: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed?

definitions.text: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed?

blocks.clueFragment: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed?
blocks.note: surface reading: an annoyed cat flicking its tail

blocks.clueFragment: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the cat is Beatrix Potter's Mrs Tabitha, whose surname describes that very jerk of the tail

explanation.walkthrough: Tabitha is the mother cat in Beatrix Potter's Tale of Tom Kitten, and her surname splits into what an irritated cat does with its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Her surname reads as a jerk of the tail plus the pronoun it, the action of an irritated cat.

clue.text: Vital part of a young marshal-to-be

blocks.note: a kid is a young child
Michel Ney became one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Some essential quality in a youngster destined to become a marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: A young Ney was a marshal-to-be; Ney was Napoleon's famous marshal.
explanation.definitionFit: This organ filters the blood and is essential to life, one of the body's vital organs.

clue.text: Old copper turned upside down by the new?

blocks.clueFragment: Old copper turned upside down by the new?
blocks.note: surface reading: a veteran policeman humiliated by a young recruit

blocks.clueFragment: Old copper turned upside down by the new?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the old penny, abbreviated d, was replaced in 1971 by the new penny, abbreviated p, which is a d flipped over

explanation.walkthrough: Before Britain's 1971 decimalisation a penny was written d, from this Roman coin's name; the new decimal penny is written p, a d turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman coin gave its initial to the old British penny, a copper coin now superseded.

clue.text: There are few fellows like him in Government

definitions.text: There are few fellows like him in Government

blocks.clueFragment: There are few fellows like him in Government
blocks.note: surface reading: praise for a rare and admirable politician

blocks.clueFragment: There are few fellows like him in Government
blocks.note: setter's reading: he is one of the few people who hold all the power

explanation.definitionFit: He belongs to a small ruling group, since the Greek root means rule by the few.

clue.text: An angel has it cooked and served cold

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a dish that is served cold

indicators.note: cooking transforms its ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavenly cook preparing a dish and serving it chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: It is boned meat or poultry pressed with jelly and eaten chilled, a classic cold buffet dish.

clue.text: Dismissed a legislator — it might cause an explosion

blocks.note: fired means sacked
taken as written
a Member of Parliament makes laws

explanation.surface: Sacking a politician could set off a political explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: This methane gas collects in coal mines and can ignite in deadly blasts.

clue.text: Citizens take in £25 in return for giving a general view

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other
in return means turned back, so the whole is written from right to left

blocks.note: cit is an old short form of citizen
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Townsfolk receiving twenty-five pounds in exchange for an overview.
explanation.definitionFit: Synoptic means presenting a summary of the whole, as the first three Gospels share a common outlook.

clue.text: Musketeer to seek gold Chinese vessel

blocks.note: Sam Small is the soldier of Stanley Holloway's monologue who refused to pick up his musket
prospectors pan river gravel looking for gold

explanation.surface: One of the musketeers sets off on a gold hunt aboard a Chinese ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Musketeer suggests Dumas, but it is Old Sam, of the music-hall piece 'Pick up tha' musket'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in Chinese harbours and rivers.

clue.text: They may be gay, yet like all flesh just grass

blocks.note: first meaning: dashing young men, in the old phrase gay young sparks
second meaning: slender leaves of grass; the Bible says all flesh is grass

explanation.surface: A reflection that merry young men are as mortal as grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All flesh is grass' is from Isaiah; gay here has its old sense of carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing young fellows are known as gay sparks, and single leaves of grass are named the same way.

clue.text: Shallow cousin was no stout fellow

blocks.note: first meaning: in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor, Justice Shallow's cousin is a foolish young suitor of this name
second meaning: thin, not plump

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about a weak, superficial relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Shallow looks like an adjective but is the name of a Shakespeare character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespeare character's name is also an adjective meaning thin, the opposite of portly.

clue.text: Wonders about distance in which car reverses

indicators.note: a car that reverses goes backwards, so its letters run right to left
in which tells us the next piece sits inside the one before it

blocks.note: miles are a measure of distance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering at the distance a car covers going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Miracles are marvels or extraordinary events, things that excite wonder.

clue.text: Indian lakes money for the basket

blocks.note: the Cree are a North American Indian people
L abbreviates lake, and also stands for pounds; 'lakes money' also plays on the lakh, an Indian sum

explanation.surface: Indian sums of money, lakhs, being spent on a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian looks like it means India, but it is a North American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket, especially one an angler uses to carry the catch.

clue.text: Foreign articles about a seaman misdescribe him

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; applied to an able seaman it misdescribes him

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article pair sits around the sailor

blocks.note: un and le are French articles
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Foreign newspapers getting a sailor's description wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The seaman is an AB, an able seaman, so calling him the opposite of able misdescribes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling an able seaman incapable gets him exactly wrong, which is why the word misdescribes him.

clue.text: Pinched — a jellyfish can't be

blocks.note: first meaning: stolen, in slang
second meaning: having the skeleton removed, impossible for a creature without one

explanation.surface: Someone tries to nip a jellyfish and finds it cannot be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stolen, and the cook's word for having had the skeleton taken out.

clue.text: Shorter than short cheese

indicators.note: shorter than means a little less long, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: brief means short

explanation.surface: A cheese described as even more compact than compact.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind, named after its home region.

clue.text: Syllabuses include some hard words

indicators.note: include some says a run of letters is held within the following word

blocks.note: the run sits inside this word

explanation.surface: School syllabuses featuring a few difficult words.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard words suggests difficult vocabulary, but it means harsh words.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting or harsh language is called abuse, as in hurling it at someone.

clue.text: The garden air is subtly charged

indicators.note: something done subtly is altered in a clever way, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The air in the garden feels faintly electric.
explanation.walkthrough: Charged suggests electricity in the air, but it means formally accused.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brought before a court and formally accused of a crime is the legal sense here.

clue.text: His the age of make-believe

blocks.note: surface reading: a child at the age of playing pretend
setter's reading: the first word is an age, the second one who makes believe he is king

explanation.walkthrough: The title belongs to James Francis Edward Stuart, who claimed the British throne in the 1700s; old is the age, and a pretender is a claimant.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the elder Stuart claimant to the throne, so a senior rival claimant to the crown.
